And in this year,
which is the year 1500
1500 of the Greeks,
there was a dispute between Sultan Qilij Arslān and his eldest son who was residing in Sebastea,
and about four thousand of the Turks who were with the son of the Sultan were killed.
Then the amīr Bahrāmshāh,
the son-in-law of the Sultan,
made peace between them.
And the Sultan removed from his presence Ikhtiyār al-Dīn Ḥasan,
his amīr ḥājib,
because he was an instigator of strife between him and his sons.
And when Ikhtiyār al-Dīn gathered his sons, his household, and his kinsmen, about two hundred horsemen,
and went and entered the meadow of Kanyūk,
the son of the Sultan sent Turcomans, and they killed him, his sons, and those who were with him.
And they cut him limb from limb,
and hung him upon the points of spears,
and carried him round about Sebastea on the day of the feast of the Cross.
And in this year, Muʿizz al-Dīn Qayṣarshāh, the son of Sultan Qilij Arslān, became ruler over Melitene.
And in this year, diverse nations of the Franks went forth in vast numbers beyond count to the city of Tyre,
and from there they came and encamped against Acre.
And when Saladin heard, he was terrified,
and dread of them fell upon him.
And he sent, summoned, and brought all his forces,
and he also went and encamped near the Franks.
And when he saw
that the Franks were increasing in strength,
and every day fresh people and provisions were coming to them by sea,
he was dismayed.
And he gathered his nobles, and they took counsel together,
and they judged it proper that they should hasten to stir up battle,
and engage the Franks before they should increase further and grow stronger.
And they prepared themselves all through that night of Friday, the beginning of the seventh month;
and when the morning broke,
they clashed with one another.
And the battle continued all day until the sun set,
and both sides held out bravely,
and spent that whole night upon their horses.
And on the Sabbath day likewise, the fire of war burned fiercely all day.
And while the Franks were busy in battle,
the northern {OCR?: ܓܲܪܒ݁ܝܵܐ} side of Acre was left vacant of the Franks,
where they had no tents.
